A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same δ-Unlearning work and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures. All 11 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2 support comparison; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original TOFU and general-benchmark experiments in Tables 2–3, plus training-trajectory and offset-strength analyses in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds statistical forgetting results and original Qwen offset-model comparisons in Table 5.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same logit-offset ensemble, freeze the target and reference models, and optimize only the second offset model using existing unlearning objectives. The Qwen experiments change model configurations, not the proposed procedure. Removing the LoRA disclosure does not establish a training-method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TOFU's forget, retain, real-author, and world-fact data, plus ARC, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, and OpenBookQA. The added Qwen experiments use retained task coverage; different model families and sizes do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds Before Unlearning and Retraining comparisons on the four general benchmarks, where v1 Table 3 reported only direct fine-tuning and δ-Unlearning. The four evaluated unlearning algorithms remain Gradient Ascent, Gradient Difference, KL Minimization, and Data Relabeling.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation with KS-test-based Forget Quality and harmonic-mean Model Utility, and adds a controlled experiment using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with 3B, 1.5B, and 0.5B offsets. The existing Llama2 configuration, ROUGE-matching criterion, five epochs, batch size 32, and α=1 remain. Zero-shot general-benchmark evaluation is newly documented, not demonstrably changed.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 and Table 5 provide a focused sensitivity analysis of offset-model capacity, testing retention and distributional forgetting with three offset sizes. The existing training trajectories, offset-strength sweep, and generated-response case study are retained.

E5.justification: V2 introduces Forget Quality based on a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and reports it in Tables 2 and 5. This adds statistical distributional assessment, but neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or variability across runs.

E6.justification: Previously reported Llama2 scores remain unchanged after matching the reorganized tables. V2 adds Forget Quality, aggregate Model Utility, general-benchmark control scores, and the Qwen results. In Table 5, offsets yield Model Utility of 48.8–52.2 versus 37.8 for direct fine-tuning, but lower Forget Quality: 4.9e-10–6.7e-6 versus 1.2e-4. These are substantive new findings, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The unlearning problem definition, logit ensemble, product-of-experts expression, and training-loss equation are unchanged. V2 adds standard empirical metric descriptions but no new theoretical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three-part contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: unlearning without updating target-model weights, competitive forgetting and retained utility, and compatibility with multiple unlearning algorithms. The added experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 removes the standalone limitations discussion, including restricted full-logit access and increased inference latency, and removes the training-efficiency rationale from Section 3.3. It adds interpretations connecting knowledge tradeoffs and weaker offsets to changed training dynamics. Section 5.2 also corrects the α=0.2 example to say unlearning is not taking effect and recommends matching inference offset strength to training.

D1.justification: V2 removes the code-access link, explicit LoRA usage, single-GPU count, 10-forget/190-retain author counts, and frozen-logit precomputation explanation. It adds the zero-shot accuracy evaluation framework and Qwen configuration details. The losses materially reduce reproducibility documentation; they do not establish that the code became unavailable or that the underlying training procedure and splits changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Feng et al. on modular knowledge access, Tianle Li et al. on long-context limitations, and Gao et al. for the evaluation framework; it removes the Hu et al. LoRA citation. The introduction newly positions the method as complementary to modular knowledge access, while the main related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose are retained. V2 locally revises the introduction, evaluation description, and results discussion; renames Section 5.1; adds Section 5.3 and acknowledgments; and removes the limitations section. Language corrections are limited, and Section 4.2 introduces an unfinished sentence beginning 'Note that while Llama2 models'.

P2.justification: V2 changes the article from two-column to single-column journal layout and substantially reorganizes the results displays. Earlier Tables 2–3 become a combined summary table and a separate retain-data table; Table 5 is added. Figure 1 is restyled, and Figure 2 gains a retraining marker. The existing trajectory curves and Figure 3's underlying results are retained.

improvement.justification: The added distributional forgetting assessment and Qwen size analysis strengthen the empirical account beyond v1's single model pairing. However, v2 removes important applicability caveats and key reproducibility information, including the code link, LoRA usage, and split counts. These material gains and losses affect different central aspects of quality, and neither clearly dominates enough to establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
